# Day 10: Countries, states and a region

## Teacher page

### Before class
Prepare the shared pieces listed above. Keep key-10.md teacher-only. Return day 9 papers, including s01-X9, with one private cue. Keep the new exit source separate until Exit ticket. Retain the record sheet and needed references.

### The day
#### 5 min. Return and repair
Return day 9's s01-X9 and s01-P9-3. Review province and territory. If many showed error E on day 9's exit, use [[s01-P10-R]] and trace one division inside Canada. Otherwise children follow their written cues and retry this fresh record independently.

#### 10 min. Countries, states and region
Whole class: review country and state from grade 3, and political map from day 1. Trace Mexico and the United States outlines. **Ask.** [[s01-K10-1]] Wait, then show [[steps:s01-K10-1]]. Separately attempt [[s01-K10-2]], then show [[steps:s01-K10-2]]. Review region from day 3's physical grouping; extend it to the Caribbean grouping. A region can include countries and other territories. Use boundaries and references, never island size, to decide categories.

#### 15 min. Supported work
Pairs attempt [[s01-P10-1]], then [[s01-P10-2]] on separate records. Each child next completes [[s01-P10-3]] before talking. Two simultaneous 90-second exchanges take three minutes. Teacher reserves five minutes for at most four children needing error E repair: contrast the country's outer boundary with a state's internal boundary. Show the teacher answer key after attempts. These practice corrections stay in the folder.

#### 5 min. Question board
Review the board routine. Every child completes [[s01-P10-4]]; collect all corrections. Hear at most two optional explanations, 45 seconds each. Public passing is allowed. Post the supported region correction.

#### 5 min. Exit ticket
Reveal Side 2 and [[s01-X10]] at each child's independent turn. Children mark both map panels and write categories on the half slip. This single linked record needs the full half slip. Collect maps and slips. Mark after class: 30 children times 40 seconds, 20 minutes. Use shown, shown with help, not yet seen per component. Return day 11 with the board correction and one cue.

### Other rooms
No printer: draw the supplied practice outlines and a separate exit set on individual paper. An enlarged paper inset replaces a screen. Read names aloud without identifying categories.

### At home
**Swap.** No copies: draw the practice maps and a separate exit set.
**Skip.** Public explanations and the class board.
- **5 min. Return.** Read day 9's cue; attempt [[s01-P10-R]].
- **10 min. Explore.** Follow the supplied Jalisco trail, then correct [[s01-K10-2]]. **Say.** "Does the Caribbean region have to be one country?" Expect: no; it groups countries and other territories.
- **15 min. Repair.** Your child attempts [[s01-P10-1]], [[s01-P10-2]] and [[s01-P10-3]]. Discuss afterward; star [[s01-P10-4]].
- **5 min. Exit ticket.** Reveal Side 2 and [[s01-X10]]. Your child marks and labels alone. Discuss afterward.

### Shorter or longer
Shorter: omit public explanations. Keep the three different practice corrections and exit. Longer: explain why a small island's size cannot tell its political category.

### Words and supports
Review: country, state, province, territory, political map, index, region and border. State: a part of our country. Border: where one country ends and the next begins. State extends here to a Mexican division. Read source references aloud; use enlarged outlines and dictated categories without category hints.

### Tomorrow
Day 11 returns day 10's exit and board correction. For error E, repair a fresh country/state boundary record. Then separate a city, county and state nesting example from a living nation's government.

### Credit
Ours. Source 10G supports countries and outlines, Source 10M states, and Source 10R the Caribbean grouping.

## Student page
### Side 1
**I can locate political places and distinguish their categories.**
